pages.text: Long, long ago, people did not have numbers written on paper.
But they still needed to count things — like animals, fruits, and tools.
So they used their fingers. One finger for one sheep.
When their fingers were not enough, they made small marks on rocks.
Each mark meant one. More marks meant more things.
Over time, people created special symbols for numbers.
These symbols made counting faster and easier.
Numbers helped people trade, build homes, and share food fairly.
As people explored the world, numbers helped them measure distance and time.
Today, numbers are everywhere — on clocks, houses, books, and even phones!
